summary.en: What the seven cases are, their questions, and the four main ones: nominative, genitive, dative and accusative.
summary.bs: Šta je sedam padeža, njihova pitanja i četiri glavna: nominativ, genitiv, dativ i akuzativ.

en.one: Bosnian and Croatian have seven cases (padeži). A case is a change in a word's ending that shows its job in the sentence.
en.explain: Each case has its questions. 1. Nominativ – ko? (tko?) šta? (što?) – the subject. 2. Genitiv – koga? čega? – of / from / without. 3. Dativ – kome? čemu? – to/for someone. 4. Akuzativ – koga? šta? (što?) – the direct object. 5. Vokativ – hej! – calling someone. 6. Lokativ – o kome? o čemu? (gdje?) – location, always after a preposition. 7. Instrumental – s kim? čim? – with whom / by means of what. Nouns, adjectives, pronouns and numbers all change.
en.example: žena (N), žene (G), ženi (D), ženu (A), ženo! (V), o ženi (L), sa ženom (I).
en.why: Because the ending shows who does what, word order is free. 'Marko voli Anu' and 'Anu voli Marko' mean the same.
en.mixup: Many learners memorise tables. It's easier to learn the questions first, then one model word for each gender.

en.one: The nominativ is the subject case and the dictionary form. Questions: ko? (tko?) šta? (što?).
en.explain: It's the form you find in the dictionary: grad, žena, selo. It's used for the subject of the sentence and after 'biti' to say what something is: 'To je moj brat.' How to spot it: ask the verb 'ko (tko) radi?' / 'šta (što) se dešava (događa)?'
en.example: 'Moja sestra radi u banci.' Ko radi? Moja sestra → nominativ.
en.why: It's your starting point: every other case is a change from the nominative.
en.mixup: The subject isn't always first: 'Danas dolazi Amir.' Ko dolazi? Amir – still nominative at the end.

en.one: The genitiv shows belonging, origin, quantity and absence. Questions: koga? čega?
en.explain: Endings: masc./neut. -a (grada, sela), fem. -e (žene, kuće). Plural: mostly -a (gradova, žena, sela). Used after: 'nema' (Nema mlijeka), quantity words (malo, mnogo, čaša – glass of: čaša vode), numbers 5+ (pet gradova), and prepositions iz (from), od (from / of), bez (without), do (until / to), kod (at someone's place), blizu (near), poslije (after), prije (before).
en.example: 'Ja sam iz Sarajeva.' 'Kafa (kava) bez šećera.' 'Idem kod mame.' 'Molim čašu vode.'
en.why: It's the most-used case after nominative and accusative, and it shows up with every 'from', 'without' and 'a glass of'.
en.mixup: English 'of' isn't always genitive: 'pričam o filmu' (I talk about the film) uses the locative.

en.one: The dativ is for the person who receives something or benefits. Questions: kome? čemu?
en.explain: Endings: masc./neut. -u (bratu, djetetu), fem. -i (sestri, ženi). Plural: -ima/-ama (studentima, sestrama). Used with verbs of giving, saying and helping: dati, poslati, reći, pomoći, pokazati, and with prepositions prema (towards), k(a) (to). Many feelings are expressed with the dative: 'Hladno mi je' (I'm cold), 'Žao mi je' (I'm sorry), 'Sviđa mi se' (I like it).
en.example: 'Dajem knjigu bratu.' Kome dajem? bratu. 'Pomažem mami.' 'Sviđa mi se ovaj grad.'
en.why: The dative turns up in feelings and likes, which you need from day one.
en.mixup: Dative and locative have the same endings in the singular. Look for a preposition: no preposition (or k, prema) → dative; u, na, o, po, pri → locative.

en.one: The akuzativ is the direct object: the person or thing the action goes to. Questions: koga? šta? (što?).
en.explain: Feminine -a → -u: žena → ženu, kafa → kafu (kava → kavu). Masculine: for things, same as nominative (vidim grad); for people and animals, same as genitive, -a (vidim brata, psa). Neuter: same as nominative (vidim selo). It's also used after u/na for movement towards a place: 'Idem u školu', 'Idem na posao'.
en.example: 'Pijem kafu (kavu).' 'Čekam autobus.' 'Volim svoga brata.' 'Idem u Mostar.'
en.why: Almost every sentence with an object uses it. It's the case you'll use most after the nominative.
en.mixup: Masculine living beings take -a: 'Vidim čovjeka', not 'Vidim čovjek'. Things don't: 'Vidim sto (stol)'.

en.one: A three-step method to identify the case of any noun.
en.explain: 1. Is there a preposition before it? The preposition narrows it down: bez/iz/od/do/kod → genitive; s(a) 'with' → instrumental; o/po/pri → locative; u/na → accusative (where to?) or locative (where?). 2. No preposition? Ask the verb: ko (tko)? → N; koga/šta (što)? → A; kome? → D; koga/čega? (of, quantity, nema) → G. 3. Check the ending against the model words: žena, žene, ženi, ženu, ženo, ženi, ženom.
en.example: 'Poslije posla dajem sestri knjigu.' poslije → genitive (posla). kome? sestri → dative. šta (što)? knjigu → accusative.
en.why: With this routine you stop guessing and can work out any sentence step by step.
en.mixup: Same ending, different cases: 'ženi' can be dative or locative. Only the question or preposition tells them apart.

q.en: Which question belongs to the dative?

explain.en: A masculine living being in the accusative takes -a.
